segments.he: ר' אברהם ז"ל אמר אפי' שרה אמנו ע"ה אם הי' אברהם אבינו ע"ה לא נותן לה פרנסה לא היתה שותקת והיתה ג"כ צועקת:
segments.en:
Concerning Rabbainu's shofar: after Rabbainu passed away, the story was known that he had told of the arousal he experienced from the shofar he heard on the first day of Elul — and his daughter came to him that Shabbos and said: "Father — I too had a great awakening from the shofar-blowing today," as the story is told in Sichos HaRan. And Rabbainu said then the Torah teaching in Likutay Moharan chapter 141 which begins: "If one merits, one will feel the pain of one's sins" — and this Torah and the prayer upon it in Likutay Tefilos chapter 85 are connected to the month of Elul.

After Rabbainu told of his awakening, Moharan'as was moved and dozed off and dreamed he was engaging with Rabbainu in the Torah of chapter 10, Ve'eileh HaMishpatim — and had a great awakening, especially in the passage about "the spirit that departs to another place." When he came to Rabbainu, Rabbainu told him of a dream he himself had had — that he wanted to hear the voice of the shofar, and heard that in a certain house they were singing and celebrating and dancing in a loud voice. And Rabbainu said: "Surely it is good to enter here to hear the voice of the shofar!" And one person said: "Is this not hinted at in Likutay Moharan chapter ten — that the commandment of the shofar is the aspect of clapping of hands and dancing? For that Torah teaches from the Zohar: 'be'terua d'ika rucha mis'abir el achar' [in the blast of the shofar a spirit is caused to pass to another place] — and through this one merits the clapping of hands and dancing. So the terua [shofar blast] is the aspect of clapping and dancing." And Rabbainu nodded his head [confirming this was true]. Present then were Reb Noson, Reb Naftali, Reb Shimon, Reb Shmuel Ayzik, and Reb Yudel.

Reb Noson wanted to tell Rabbainu his own dream — that he had been engaging with Rabbainu in the Torah of chapter ten. But before he could, Rabbainu said: "You do not need to tell me — I myself know, for you are the one who answered and said the proof from be'terua d'ika rucha." After this, Reb Noson took Rabbainu's shofar and would blow it himself the entire month of Elul — and only on Rosh HaShanah would he give the shofar to the community. And specifically Reb Meir Leib Blechir would blow on it. After Moharan'as's passing, Reb Yitzchak son of Moharan'as took the shofar — and when he traveled to the Holy Land he took it with him to Tzfas the holy city. And the shofar remained in Tzfas — and also Rabbainu's chalat [garment] and belt remained there.
